title: Who makes the music at Rockstar
short: The habit started in a record company. Sam Houser began in BMG's London post room in 1990, BMG's games arm published the first Grand Theft Auto, and GTA's radio was pitched in Scotland by Colin Anderson of DMA Design's sound department so one musician's demos across many genres could all survive. Since then a small in-house team has picked, hosted, written and mastered the stations, with Sam Houser as the documented final word on taste. Dan Houser left in March 2020, and Lazlow later that year, on a date nobody quite agrees on.

title: The radio, game by game: 1997 to 2006
short: In the first two games almost everything on air was written in-house under fake band names. GTA III (2001) mixed those acts with licensed music and talk radio, Vice City (2002) went all in on licensed 1980s tracks, and San Andreas (2004) grew to 10 music stations with celebrity DJs. The two "Stories" games of 2005 and 2006 went back to Liberty City and Vice City with fresh playlists on the same formulas.

title: The radio, game by game: GTA IV and GTA V
short: GTA IV (2008) gave Liberty City 19 stations and handed most of the microphones to real musicians, from Iggy Pop to Karl Lagerfeld, and its two episodes added three stations of their own. GTA V (2013) launched with 15 music stations and 240 licensed songs, grew by about 165 tracks on the 2014 consoles, and GTA Online kept bolting on whole stations through MOTOMAMI Los Santos in December 2021.

title: Talk radio: Chatterbox to Chakra Attack
short: Talk radio exists in Grand Theft Auto because, by Dan Houser's own account, it was the cheapest way to fill hours of driving in GTA III (2001). Written mostly by Houser and Lazlow Jones, it became the series' sharpest satire: one call-in station in Liberty City, two in Vice City, a whole network of shows on San Andreas's WCTR, three political stations in GTA IV and a left/right split by county in GTA V. Lazlow, who played a steadily sadder version of himself, left Rockstar in 2020 after nine GTA games, in a month that depends on who you read.

title: The lore: fake ads, fake bands and the bits people quote
short: Between the songs sit fake ads for parody brands, bands that exist only in the game, real stars voicing invented DJs, and news bulletins about what you just did in a mission. Most of it was written by Dan Houser and Lazlow Jones from GTA III (2001) until Lazlow left Rockstar in 2020, and a good share of what fans can recite has never been confirmed outside the fan wikis.

title: The scores: music written for the games
short: For its first decade, Grand Theft Auto's original music was mostly in-house songs credited to fictional bands, played on the radio rather than under the action. GTA V (2013) brought a full original score, which Rockstar called its first fully collaborative score, built by Tangerine Dream, Woody Jackson, The Alchemist and Oh No as layered stems that react to play. Red Dead Redemption, Red Dead Redemption 2, Max Payne 3 and GTA Online all got scores of their own, and Justice is scoring GTA VI.

title: GTA Online: the club, the label and the residency
short: From late 2017, GTA Online stopped being a game that licensed music and started acting like a venue, a radio network and a record label. The After Hours update (July 2018) let players own nightclubs where four real DJs held motion-captured residencies, and Cayo Perico (December 2020) added a second club, The Music Locker, plus three new stations. In 2021 came CircoLoco Records, the Media Player and six new Dr. Dre tracks that premiered inside the game weeks before streaming.

title: CircoLoco Records: Rockstar's label with a Monday party
short: CircoLoco Records is a record label run as a partnership between CircoLoco, the Monday party at DC10 in Ibiza, and Rockstar Games, announced on May 24, 2021. It opened with *Monday Dreamin'*, a 20-track compilation whose four EPs became hidden collectibles in GTA Online in July 2021, and since 2024 it has turned into a chart label for house and tech house. A "CircoLoco Records Radio" station for GTA VI exists only in a leak; Rockstar did not name one in its October 2026 station reveal.

title: Why songs disappear: licenses, expiry and removals
short: A song on a GTA radio station is rented, not owned. Each licensed track needs permission for both the composition and the recording, usually for a fixed term, and when those permissions run out Rockstar patches the song out of the versions it still sells. That has happened to Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and, in September 2026, GTA V - a game Take-Two says has sold nearly 235 million units (official, November 2026). GTA VI arrives on November 19, 2026, with a commissioned 34-track album beside its radio, and nobody has said how its music deals are built.

title: GTA VI: the music at launch
short: Grand Theft Auto VI came out on November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, after two delays. Launch-day lists count 22 radio stations - 20 music, two talk - with hosts including Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Robyn and two members of Slayer, plus five on-demand podcast series, a series first. Rockstar and Atlantic's 34-track original album arrived the same day, and Justice's score follows as its own album on December 11. Rockstar has not published full station playlists, so the song lists here come from the press, and they do not fully agree.

title: Test yourself, and where to dig next
short: Quiz yourself on everything above, learn the trade's vocabulary, run the timeline from 1997 to now, then dig into the best outside sources and the questions nobody has answered yet.
